No evidence exists of any other person-to-person digital payment mechanism in Eritrea.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: No credible evidence of digital/instant payment system, real-time payments, mobile money interoperability, or nationwide infrastructure found after extensive searches (GSMA datasets exclude Eritrea, EriTel no service, AfricaNenda notes Eritrea as only African country w/o IPS plans). Cash-dominant; limited banking/mobile (22% connections). Searches: instant payment, real-time, digital infra, mobile money, central bank payments.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Re-verified with a March 2026 Fintech Times ecosystem review, which confirms Eritrea 'does not yet have a fully functioning fintech ecosystem', with mobile wallets linked to the state telecom operator EriTel described as 'emerging' and 'still limited in functionality' rather than an operational instant/real-time payment system. This is corroborated by Eritel's own website, which describes only voice services and a basic airtime-transfer code, and by PAPSS's June 2026 coverage document, which does not list Eritrea as a participant. Confirms the existing score of 1 (No) with fresher, stronger sources.
revised_comments: Eritrea has not established an instant or real-time payment system. The financial sector remains cash-dominated and centralised around a small number of state-owned banks, with more than 70% of the population unbanked. Nascent mobile-wallet functionality linked to the state telecommunications operator, EriTel, is emerging but remains limited to basic services such as airtime transfer, and the country is not a participant in the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS).

revision_notes: World Bank Global Findex/G20 FI data records no value (N/A) for Eritrea, and no dedicated survey of active digital payment users was found. A March 2026 Fintech Times review reports mobile penetration of under 60% of population (World Bank 2022 data, ranked 191st of 209 countries), an unbanked rate above 70%, and total online commerce/digital payment volumes of under USD10 million a year — consistent with active digital payment usage well below 20% of the adult population. Recalculated from Unknown to 1 (<20%) on this basis rather than left unscored.
revised_comments: Active use of digital payment systems in Eritrea is very low, estimated at well under 20% of the adult population. Mobile phone penetration stood at under 60% as of 2022 (191st of 209 countries ranked by the World Bank), more than 70% of Eritreans remain unbanked, and total digital payment and e-commerce volumes are estimated at under USD10 million a year, reflecting the early stage of the country's digital financial services.
